question: Under the proposed National Building Research Institute law, how long does an employee have to decide whether to decline the offered position after being notified?
answer:
**Six months** — the opt-out must be exercised "within six months from the date on which he was offered employment in the Institute" [629/2025 §33(2)(b)].

- This is the newest version: National Building Research Institute Bill (Bill, 2025-08-19); the GS of 2025-07-17 [621/2025 §33] and 2024-09-03 [551/2024 §33] carry identical wording.
- The same clause provides that an officer who declines "shall be paid compensation under a voluntary retirement scheme," approved by the Minister and the Minister of Finance [629/2025 §33(2)(c)].

Caveats: The text frames this as a six-month window to "opt out," not expressly as a deadline to "decide"; no separate decision-period is stated. No answer on any other timeline.

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Licensing of Shipping Agents, Freight Forwarders, Non‑Vessel Operating Common Carriers and Container Operators Act, how is the Act’s long title changed regarding the mention of container operators?
answer:
It removes them: the long title's words "freight forwarders, non-vessel operating common carriers, and container operators" are substituted with "freight forwarders and non-vessel operating common carriers" [658/2025 §2].

- So the words "and container operators" are deleted from the principal Act's long title (Act No. 10 of 1972) [658/2025 §2].
- Text is identical in the Bill version, published 2026-01-20 [005/2026 §1]; the GS version is dated 2025-12-12 [658/2025 §1].

Caveats: none material; the evidence quotes the amendment in mixed case, but the substitution wording is clear.

question: Under the amended Rubber Control Act, who is defined as the “Director‑General”?
answer:
The new definition in §52 reads: “**Director-General**” means the Director-General of the Rubber Development Department, “appointed or deemed to have been appointed under this Act” [494/2024 §6] — the same text appears in the 2025 versions [595/2025 §6; 620/2025 §6].

- It replaces the repealed definition of “Controller” in section 52 of the principal enactment (Chapter 436) [494/2024 §6].
- Existing references to “Controller”/“Rubber Controller” in other laws and documents are read as references to the “Director-General of the Rubber Development Department” [620/2025 §2(2)].
- Newest version: Bill 620/2025 (2025-07-09); GS 595/2025 (2025-05-28); GS 494/2024 (2024-05-29).

Caveats: The “deemed to have been appointed” formula is quoted, not interpreted here; no other duties are set out in §6.

question: Under the proposed Companies (Amendment) Act, what remedy is available to a company whose name has been struck off, and what are the effects on its former assets?
answer:
The company may apply to court (with the Attorney-General made a party) within ten years, and the court may permit re-registration and order return of the property that had vested in the State. Newest text: Companies (Amendment) GS [582/2025 §17], 2025-04-24 (identical in 606/2025); same provision in [541/2024 §15], 2024-08-06 (identical in 563/2024).

- Deadline: "before the expiry of a period of ten years" from the amendment Act's operation, showing cause why it could not comply with subsection (1) [582/2025 §17].
- On re-registration, the court may "make an order for the return to the company of all property previously vested in the State" [582/2025 §17].
- Limits: third parties acquiring rights from the State "in good faith shall not be affected", and where property is destroyed/damaged or possession not taken, "the State shall not be liable to any party" [582/2025 §17].

Caveats: Both are Gazette (GS) versions; no presented Bill text is in evidence, and the 2025 and 2024 drafts differ only in wording of the ten-year start point.

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Judicature Act, how are the retirement ages for judges and magistrates being changed?
answer:
The 2026 GS bill amends section 6: one retirement age rises from “sixty-one years” to “sixty-three years,” while “all other Judges and Magistrates” retire at “sixty-two years” [058/2026 §3].

- The substitution is expressly ““sixty-one years”” → ““sixty-three years”” [058/2026 §3].
- The new subsection (4) states: “the age of retirement of all other Judges and Magistrates shall be sixty-two years” [058/2026 §3].

Caveat: the passage does not identify which judicial office subsection (3) covers; identical text also appears in 064/2026 [058/2026 §3].

question: Which 2025 bill sought to modify the 1988 Sri Lankan law that imposes a tax on gambling activities?
answer:
The evidence does not show any 2025 bill that amends the Betting and Gaming Levy Act, No. 40 of 1988; the only 2025 bill in the passages is the Gambling Regulatory Authority Bill (613/2025, Bill dated 2025-06-17), which merely *refers to* that Act.

- That Bill treats a conviction or contravention under the "Betting and Gaming Levy Act, No. 40 of 1988" as grounds for cancelling [613/2025 §30] or suspending [613/2025 §29] a licence.
- Identical text appears in 594/2025 [613/2025 §30], so the two versions do not differ in these passages.
- No clause in the evidence actually amends, repeals or changes the levy imposed by the 1988 Act.

Caveats: The amending provisions, if any, are not in the evidence supplied; I cannot identify a bill that modifies the 1988 levy from these passages.
